A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NTL research and contain complete, matchable main text and Appendix A. Text, equations, tables, figures and the qualitative example support reliable comparison despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original model-training and evaluation results on mathematical tasks, humor-score regression, reading comprehension and GSM8K, including appendix ablations and error analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and their outcomes in Section 4 and Appendix A.

M1.justification: The NTL-Lp and Wasserstein formulations, their combination with cross-entropy, and Algorithms A1–A2 are unchanged. The added RAFT acknowledgment and software-package information introduce no method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same DeepMind mathematics, integer-multiplication, rJokes, MultiRC and GSM8K coverage, including the same interpolation and extrapolation scenarios.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain CE, Regression Transformer, xVal, Gaussian Cross Entropy, regression-head models and the appendix encoding baselines. RAFT is newly discussed as concurrent work but is not added to an evaluated comparison.

E3.justification: Sections 3–4 and Appendix A.6 retain the same splits, preprocessing, tokenization conditions, model sizes, training budgets and evaluation metrics. No existing protocol is revised or new evaluation introduced.

E4.justification: The loss-weight, Gaussian-smoothing, tokenizer and squashing ablations are unchanged. Sample-efficiency analyses, GSM8K error histograms, digit-boundary analyses and Example 1 also retain the same evidence.

E5.justification: The mean-and-standard-deviation reporting, error bars and stated run counts are unchanged throughout the main text and appendix. No new uncertainty-estimation practice or statistical test is reported.

E6.justification: Numerical tables and plotted results match. For example, both versions report CE/NTL-WAS interpolation accuracies of 0.64/0.75 in Table 1 and GSM8K accuracies of 13.5%/17.7% in Table 9. Appendix results and qualitative outputs also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10, the Wasserstein simplifications, the nonunique-minimum counterexample and the xVal normalization derivation are unchanged. The revised Lp discussion adds attribution without changing the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution statements and conclusion retain the same core claims about numerical performance, negligible overhead, regression-head parity, preserved text performance and scaling to 3B parameters.

C2.justification: The interpretations of xVal behavior, tokenization effects and generalization remain unchanged. Both versions retain the nonunique-minimum and equal-digit-weight limitations, the same future directions and the same Impact Statement.

D1.justification: v2 supplies project and development-code links. v3 additionally documents the ntloss PyPI package, distinguishes the usage repository from full-experiment reproduction code, and provides demo and video pointers in Further Resources. Implementation and training details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Lukasik et al. (2025), explicitly acknowledging that NTL-MSE was also proposed as RAFT in concurrent work and describing its regression application. This is a focused update to attribution and research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 locally edits the abstract, training-objective motivation and NTL-Lp explanation, updates the running header and adds Further Resources. The main narrative and appendix organization otherwise remain intact.

P2.justification: The new resources block changes page 9's layout and moves the Impact Statement onto page 10, with subsequent reference pagination shifting. Existing figures and tables retain their designs and content; the appendix shifts by one page.

improvement.justification: v3 improves attribution by explicitly acknowledging the concurrent RAFT formulation and makes software use and experiment reproduction easier to distinguish through the ntloss documentation and Further Resources section. These are useful, limited gains; the methods, empirical evidence and stated limitations remain unchanged.
